name: github
description: Work with GitHub repos, issues, PRs, and Actions through the GitHub API.
prompt:
Work with GitHub through a connected GitHub API integration, called via
call_api. The integration owns the base URL (https://api.github.com) and the
auth token — you supply the path. call_api advertises the valid integration
id; use that id for every request.

HEADERS — the auth header is added for you. On each call set:
    Accept: application/vnd.github+json
    X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28

KEEP RESPONSES SMALL — this is the most important habit. GitHub list
endpoints return large JSON arrays that waste context, and call_api writes
oversized bodies to a file instead of returning them. Prefer:
    - a small per_page (e.g. 10–20), never the default dump
    - the most specific endpoint for what you need (a single issue, not all
      issues, when you know the number)
    - GraphQL (POST /graphql with {"query": ..., "variables": ...}) when you
      need a few fields off several objects — it returns only the fields you
      ask for, which is far cheaper than filtering a fat REST response.
If a response gets written to a file, treat that as a signal to re-query
more narrowly rather than reading the whole dump.

PAGINATION — per_page (max 100) + page. The response's Link header carries
rel="next"; stop once you have enough rather than walking every page.

WRITES — creating or editing anything (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) requires the
integration to be connected read-write. A read-only error means the user
granted read access only; report that instead of retrying.

COMMON ENDPOINTS (replace {owner}/{repo}/{n}):
    Who am I           GET  /user
    Repo info          GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}
    List issues        GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=20
    One issue          GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}
    Create issue       POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues            {title, body}
    Comment            POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/comments {body}
    List PRs           GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open&per_page=20
    One PR             GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}
    PR changed files   GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files?per_page=30
    Create PR          POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls   {title, head, base, body}
    Review a PR        POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews {event, body}
    CI on a commit     GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs
    Actions runs       GET  /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?per_page=10
    Search issues/PRs  GET  /search/issues?q=repo:{owner}/{repo}+is:open

Note issues and PRs share the /issues comment and search surface — a PR is an
issue for commenting and searching, but has its own /pulls endpoints for diff,
files, and review.
